correctness.rationale: For selected (i,j), outside degree is n+m-r_i-c_j, and domination is exactly full coverage in at least one orientation. Put p=max(1,n-k), u=max(1,m-k). The row-cover and column-cover bounds are mp and nu respectively, both attained by complete slabs in the corresponding orientations. At the smaller bound only its winning orientation(s) can occur; equality forces r_i=p in the row-cover orientation, and then every occupied column satisfies c_j>=m+n-k-p, which is also sufficient. If p=n-k>=1, each occupied column is full; if p=1, these are exactly maps from rows to columns with the stated lower fibre threshold. The column orientation is symmetric. This reproduces all regimes, including the strict rectangular large-k inequality m<n, the intermediate tie (one per column and full-column slabs cannot intersect), square k=q-1 (a single full row or column) and k>=2q-2 (permutations are the overlap). The factorial-weighted product counts all labelled assignments without quotienting. Phi is defined on positive integer arguments and can be zero for general t>b; this does not affect any claim about the minimum sets. The frozen exhaustive script, verification notes and output were read, not executed; the proof handles unbounded sizes and capacities.

evidence: Equation (1) is rho_i+kappa_j>=m+n-k for every selected cell. The published proof says every dominating set covers all rows or columns and gives the two lower bounds by summing per-row or per-column lower bounds. The smaller bound is the exact minimum.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For any optimal row cover the earlier row bound must equal the known optimum, and every row therefore has occupancy p=max(1,n-k); (1) then gives exactly the single common threshold m+n-k-p on nonempty columns. The transposed statement handles optimal column covers. With p>1 the threshold forces slabs; with p=1 this is a direct labelled map restriction. At the tie retain both orientations, excluding permutations exactly when (1) excludes them. Multiplying ordinary labelled-fibre exponential generating functions and taking the coefficient gives precisely Phi. These are direct equality and counting operations on the prior equations, not a new structural step.

value.rationale: The labelled optimizer count is a natural quantity, but here the additional regimes only unpack known sharp occupancy bounds by equality and use standard labelled-fibre extraction. Transition, tie, and high-capacity shapes all follow from those same published equations without a new invariant, nonroutine counting argument, or additional structure. The complete presentation may be convenient, but no independent scientific remainder to repair was established.
